articles.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants.
Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement.

Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO).
Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression.
The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said.

Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad.

“Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said.

The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.
The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

fullParagraphs: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department
Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris.

According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district.
Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions.

S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs.

He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said.

Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife.
“These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said.

According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection).

Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms.

The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support.

Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models.

On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models.

The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model.
Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API).

An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use.

The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B.
Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.
Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.title: Assam CM downplays ‘fight’ between two IPS officers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The confrontation occurred at an Assam Police battalion headquarters in the western part of the State on November 22, 2026
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) downplayed an alleged clash between two senior Indian Police Service officers at a party as a “personal fight”.

The incident, involving a Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) and a Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), occurred at an Assam Police battalion in the western part of the State on Sunday night (November 22, 2026).

“There was a fight between two persons at a private programme. We have nothing to do here, as it was personal and had no connection with the Police Department. Sometimes, we also end up having arguments,” the Chief Minister told journalists on the sidelines of an official event.
“We would have done something had it happened during official duty. I have no comment on a personal matter,” he said.
According to reports, the DIG in question was among several senior police officers invited to a party the SSP had organised.
The DIG and the SSP allegedly quarrelled during the event. It turned physical, reportedly leaving the SSP injured.
Another senior IPS officer, reportedly assigned by Director General of Police Harmeet Singh, resolved the matter.
The trigger for the fight could not be ascertained. Police did not issue any statement.

articles.title: Juvenile Justice Board Hears Bail Plea of Child in Conflict with Law After High Court Rejection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene

The Juvenile Justice Board is hearing a bail application under Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, submitted by a Child in Conflict with Law (CCL) concerning C.R. No.58/2026 at Tilak Nagar Police Station, which involves a collision on February 5, 2026, that caused death and disability, following orders from the Sessions Court and the Bombay High Court that cancelled bail and required placement in a centre for reformation.

The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene, leading the Sessions Court to set aside the bail order of March 6, 2026, on July 31, 2026, and the Bombay High Court to reject the revision on September 9, 2026, in Criminal Revision Application .

The Board noted an application dated October 21, 2026, where the CCL admitted that a paper presented as an examination timetable on October 9, 2026, did not belong to him because the paper contained subjects from a course under a scheme while the admission receipt of the CCL indicated enrollment in a course with a fee structure, and the confirmation for the paper came from the father of the CCL, who is a co-accused with a challenge to bail, and the Board had asked for confirmation on three occasions before receiving the confirmation from the father.

The report from the police stated that the CCL drove a KIA Seltos motorcar without a licence for driving and collided with a scooter on February 5, 2026, resulting in the death of Dhrumil Patel on February 15, 2026, and causing disability to the survivor, with the chargesheet filed on July 14, 2026, under Sections 281, 125, 125(A), 125(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, read with Sections 184 and 199 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998, and Section 105 of the BNS.

The CCL argued that the investigation is complete and no recovery is pending, that the deletion of the account on Instagram is attributed to CCL No.2, that the meeting on February 8, 2026, involved mediators from the community and did not involve any attempt to withdraw the complaint, and that the conditions imposed by the Board did not prohibit entry into Ghatkopar, while the prosecution and the survivor argued that the CCL may contact individuals with records showing conviction, commit offenses, and pressurize witnesses, that the application seeks a review of the order from the High Court without a change in circumstances, and that the conduct of the CCL in evading the process and the submission of a paper that did not belong to the CCL does not support the grant of bail.

The CCL stated that the parents are ready to take responsibility for education, residence, and counseling, and the CCL completed the Higher Secondary Certificate Examination in the Commerce stream with a score of 74.83 percent and secured admission to the Bachelor of Commerce Programme for the year 2026-27 at KPB Hinduja College of Commerce. The survivor contended that the CCL did not comply with the directions of the Board, the CCL was not found at the address provided, the mother stated she did not know the whereabouts of the CCL, the father stated the CCL was at a location and did not produce the CCL on two occasions, and the CCL was produced on September 20, 2026, which the survivor stated was not a surrender without force.

articles.title: Keralam govt. forms search committee to find experts for fresh Vizhinjam erosion study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Move follows the Kerala High Court’s decision to invalidate the report of the previous expert committee over conflict-of-interest concerns

The State government has constituted a four-member search committee to identify experts for a fresh panel tasked with examining whether the construction of the Vizhinjam International Seaport has caused coastal erosion and recommending specific measures to address any such erosion observed in the port’s zone of influence. The move follows the Kerala High Court’s decision to invalidate the report of the previous expert committee over conflict-of-interest concerns.

The search committee comprises the Managing Director of Vizhinjam International Seaport Limited (VISL), Director of the Environment department, Director of the Fisheries department, and the Chief Engineer of the Major Irrigation department. It has been tasked with identifying and recommending suitable experts for a fresh, independent panel, ensuring that none of the proposed members has any conflict of interest.

Last month, the High Court invalidated the report of an expert committee constituted by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government to study coastal erosion allegedly caused by the port project. The court ruled that the report should not be acted upon, citing conflicts of interest involving some of its members.

The previous expert committee, constituted in 2022 following protests by fishers against the port construction, was headed by M.D. Kudale, former Additional Director of the Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS), Pune along with members Riji John, Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies, Kochi; Tejal Kanitkar, Associate Professor at the School of Natural Sciences and Engineering, National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS), Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru; and P.K. Chandramohan, former Chief Engineer of Kandla Port Trust.

The committee’s report attributed coastal erosion on the northern side of the port primarily to natural causes, including cyclones. However, the petitioners who challenged the report contended that port construction had caused substantial erosion on the northern side and accretion on the southern side. They also questioned the impartiality of the committee, alleging that some members had prior associations with the port project.

Mr. Kudale, for instance, had been serving as an expert member of the technical sub-committee for the development of Vizhinjam Seaport Ltd since 2012, whereas Mr. Chandramohan had been working as president (technical) of a company allegedly associated with Adani Enterprises, the port’s concessionaire, according to the petitioners.

The High Court subsequently directed the State government not to act upon the committee’s final report and to constitute a fresh, independent expert panel to undertake the prescribed studies, ensuring that its members had no conflicts of interest. The present United Democratic Front (UDF) government, which was in the Opposition during the fishers’ agitation, had supported the their demand to suspend the port construction, citing concerns that the project had aggravated coastal erosion.

The search committee comprises the Managing Director of Vizhinjam International Seaport Limited (VISL), Director of the Environment department, Director of the Fisheries department, and the Chief Engineer of the Major Irrigation department. It has been tasked with identifying and recommending suitable experts for a fresh, independent panel, ensuring that none of the proposed members has any conflict of interest.

Last month, the High Court invalidated the report of an expert committee constituted by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government to study coastal erosion allegedly caused by the port project. The court ruled that the report should not be acted upon, citing conflicts of interest involving some of its members.

The previous expert committee, constituted in 2022 following protests by fishers against the port construction, was headed by M.D. Kudale, former Additional Director of the Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS), Pune along with members Riji John, Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies, Kochi; Tejal Kanitkar, Associate Professor at the School of Natural Sciences and Engineering, National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS), Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru; and P.K. Chandramohan, former Chief Engineer of Kandla Port Trust.

The committee’s report attributed coastal erosion on the northern side of the port primarily to natural causes, including cyclones. However, the petitioners who challenged the report contended that port construction had caused substantial erosion on the northern side and accretion on the southern side. They also questioned the impartiality of the committee, alleging that some members had prior associations with the port project.

Mr. Kudale, for instance, had been serving as an expert member of the technical sub-committee for the development of Vizhinjam Seaport Ltd since 2012, whereas Mr. Chandramohan had been working as president (technical) of a company allegedly associated with Adani Enterprises, the port’s concessionaire, according to the petitioners.

The High Court subsequently directed the State government not to act upon the committee’s final report and to constitute a fresh, independent expert panel to undertake the prescribed studies, ensuring that its members had no conflicts of interest. The present United Democratic Front (UDF) government, which was in the Opposition during the fishers’ agitation, had supported the their demand to suspend the port construction, citing concerns that the project had aggravated coastal erosion.

articles.title: Human Metabolic Chamber inaugurated at CMC in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer
A state-of-the-art Human Metabolic Chamber was inaugurated at Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore to advance research on nutrition, diabetes, obesity, and metabolic health.

According to a press release, the initiative was a joint collaboration of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the CMC. The facility was opened by Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

The initiative brings together two of India’s premier institutions - combining TIFR’s strengths in fundamental and interdisciplinary science with CMC Vellore’s expertise in clinical medicine and metabolic research.

Anchored by TIFR’s Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development & Aging (ARUMDA) and CMC’s Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, the collaboration will help address questions on how the body uses energy, and how this varies across diverse populations, diets, and lifestyles in India.

The chamber complements the National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research, which ARUMDA established last year. Together, the two facilities allow researchers to link molecular and biochemical measurements with how the body uses energy. This ability to study metabolism at both levels places the initiative at the forefront of Indian research on metabolic diseases and aging.

The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer. These measurements reveal the total energy expenditure and how the body switches between using fat and carbohydrates across meals, activity, and sleep.

By analysing metabolism over an extended daily cycle, the chamber offers a more comprehensive picture than a brief measurement alone. It enables researchers to examine how energy use changes over time and under carefully defined study conditions. This capability is particularly important in India, whose diverse populations, dietary patterns, and lifestyles remain under-represented in global reference data.

Measurements generated through the facility can help refine the understanding of energy and nutrient requirements, and strengthen the evidence underpinning strategies against metabolic disease and malnutrition, the release said.

articles.title: Under Nishant’s leadership, the future of the party remains bright for next 30 years, says Sanjay Jha

fullParagraphs: Mr. Jha also said that former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.
Janata Dal (United) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) celebrated Sushasan Diwas (Good governance Day) to mark the day Nitish Kumar began his first full term as the Bihar Chief Minister.

JD(U) National President Nitish Kumar also attended the main programme as a chief guest organised at the State headquarters office in Patna along with his son Nishant Kumar and Sanjay Jha, National Working president of the party.
Mr. Kumar also saw his sand art displayed in the office premises. Mr. Kumar was welcomed by party workers while showering rose petals on him.

Mr. Jha while addressing the party workers, said that the new generation needs to know what conditions were like in Bihar in 2005 and how Nitish Kumar ji worked to take the state forward, with good governance, development and social justice at the centre.
‘Nitish Samvad’ (Nitish Dialogue) events were also organized in every district where JD(U) leaders spoke about the works done by Mr. Kumar.

“Nitish Kumar ji will be remembered for his work for thousands of years. Bihar needed a leader who would understand its suffering, restore its lost dignity and take it forward on a new path of development. On November 24, 2005, a new era of good governance began in Bihar under the leadership of Nitish Kumar ji,”Mr. Jha said.

He further said, “The challenges Bihar faced before 2005 are no secret. From law and order to education, healthcare, roads and electricity, the state was in a worrying state on almost every measure of development. Even Biharis, living in other states, were reluctant to reveal their identity. But through his firm resolve, clear vision and systematic efforts, Nitish Kumar ji has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.”
Mr. Jha asserted that today, being called a Bihari is no longer an insult, but a source of pride and self-respect as Bihar has established a new identity for itself in many areas of development.
He also pointed out that the impact of Nitish Kumar work will endure for many generations to come.
“His presence will continue to inspire all of us to carry forward his commitment to building a developed, prosperous and self-reliant Bihar of his dreams,”Mr. Jha said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

articles.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, U.S. jury finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds

A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.
However, jurors acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy to steal intellectual property from American companies.
The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which U.S. prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Lawyers for the company said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn't stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.
The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations.
Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology theft. Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company's networking device, the indictment said. Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.

articles.title: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ’s ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar’s leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees

Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
Editorial | Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice

The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.

Myanmar's government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Mr. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.

Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Mr. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.
He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.
Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said.
A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on September 29, he said.
Malaysia had secured a guarantee of a “safe and dignified return” for those repatriated, Mr. Anwar said.
“So far, based on monitoring by Malaysian intelligence, none of the 10,476 individuals have been subjected to any form of pressure,” he said.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ’s ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar’s leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees

Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.

Editorial | Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice

The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.

Myanmar's government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Mr. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.

Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Mr. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.

He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.

Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said.

A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on September 29, he said.

Malaysia had secured a guarantee of a “safe and dignified return” for those repatriated, Mr. Anwar said.

“So far, based on monitoring by Malaysian intelligence, none of the 10,476 individuals have been subjected to any form of pressure,” he said.

articles.title: CM to open ‘Vision Koyilandy Conclave 2026’ on Nov. 27
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The aim of the event is to conceive projects in sectors such as education, health, transport, agriculture, industry, tourism, and infrastructure development
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will open ‘Vision Koyilandy Conclave 2026’, an event to chalk out future development plans for the Koyilandy Assembly constituency in Kozhikode district, on November 27.

articles.title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Saudi capital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia

Two Indians and three Nepalese nationals were among 11 people injured on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) when Yemen's Houthi militia targeted a tower in the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital, authorities said.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said 11 people were injured after the tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia.
Those injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, it said.

It added that competent authorities immediately responded to the incident, implemented all approved procedures and measures for handling such situations, and took the necessary measures to protect lives and property.
The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also confirmed that two Indian nationals sustained injuries in the attack.
In a post on X, it said further details are being ascertained and all possible assistance will be extended to the injured persons and their families.
Earlier, Saudi-led Coalition Spokesperson Maj Gen Turki Al Malki said a tower had been targeted in the financial district and that competent authorities were responding at the site.
Meanwhile, the Indian embassy also asked Indian nationals residing in the Gulf country to abide by local rules and regulations.
The Houthis have in the past claimed responsibility for attacks on Riyadh.

articles.title: IRISET takes Kavach training to campuses, signs MoUs with 26 engineering colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the rollout of the indigenous train protection system ‘Kavach’ gaining pace, the Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET) is taking its training efforts beyond the Railways, partnering 26 engineering colleges to build a wider pool of skilled professionals.

Of the 26 institutions that signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with IRISET, eight have introduced open elective courses on Kavach, the indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system.

Addressing the institute’s annual day celebrations on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), Director General Piush Kumar Gupta said Kavach remains IRISET’s primary training focus. A two-week, design-oriented course has emerged as one of its most sought-after programmes among signalling and telecommunications professionals. So far, 187 officers and 1,031 supervisors have undergone training in these courses.

A one-week crash course conducted last year trained 542 Signal and Telecommunications (S&T) officers to support the rapid rollout of Kavach across the railway network. The institute also conducted 14 customised courses on fitting Kavach equipment in locomotives for officers and supervisors from electric loco sheds and production units, benefiting 315 participants.

In addition, 56 specialised programmes on signalling and Kavach were organised for 3,150 Chief Loco Inspectors (CLIs). IRISET also uploaded 18 online courses covering Kavach, signalling, telecommunications and information technology, with a combined duration of over 30 hours, on the iGOT Karmayogi portal. These courses have benefited more than 46,000 employees.
To meet emerging technological requirements, the institute introduced five new courses covering cloud computing, big data analytics, data science, AI applications and cyber security.
Established in 1957, IRISET conducted 261 training programmes for over 7,000 participants, recording a 50% increase in trainee-days over the previous year.

It also trained 343 apprentices, including 175 signal engineers, 115 telecom engineers and 53 design engineers. Another 291 apprentices and 53 executives of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd (DFCCIL) are currently undergoing training.

Its 20-part webinar series attracted over 3,200 railway and industry personnel. Besides mandatory courses on electronic interlocking, automatic block signalling, VoIP-based exchanges and LTE, the institute conducted practical and appreciation courses for 110 Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS) Traffic probationers and 60 B.Tech students of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. Faculty development programmes on AI and data science were also organised.

With the rollout of the indigenous train protection system ‘Kavach’ gaining pace, the Indian Railways Institute of Signal Engineering and Telecommunications (IRISET) is taking its training efforts beyond the Railways, partnering 26 engineering colleges to build a wider pool of skilled professionals.

Of the 26 institutions that signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with IRISET, eight have introduced open elective courses on Kavach, the indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system.

Addressing the institute’s annual day celebrations on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), Director General Piush Kumar Gupta said Kavach remains IRISET’s primary training focus. A two-week, design-oriented course has emerged as one of its most sought-after programmes among signalling and telecommunications professionals. So far, 187 officers and 1,031 supervisors have undergone training in these courses.

A one-week crash course conducted last year trained 542 Signal and Telecommunications (S&T) officers to support the rapid rollout of Kavach across the railway network. The institute also conducted 14 customised courses on fitting Kavach equipment in locomotives for officers and supervisors from electric loco sheds and production units, benefiting 315 participants.

In addition, 56 specialised programmes on signalling and Kavach were organised for 3,150 Chief Loco Inspectors (CLIs). IRISET also uploaded 18 online courses covering Kavach, signalling, telecommunications and information technology, with a combined duration of over 30 hours, on the iGOT Karmayogi portal. These courses have benefited more than 46,000 employees.

To meet emerging technological requirements, the institute introduced five new courses covering cloud computing, big data analytics, data science, AI applications and cyber security.

Established in 1957, IRISET conducted 261 training programmes for over 7,000 participants, recording a 50% increase in trainee-days over the previous year.

It also trained 343 apprentices, including 175 signal engineers, 115 telecom engineers and 53 design engineers. Another 291 apprentices and 53 executives of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd (DFCCIL) are currently undergoing training.

Its 20-part webinar series attracted over 3,200 railway and industry personnel. Besides mandatory courses on electronic interlocking, automatic block signalling, VoIP-based exchanges and LTE, the institute conducted practical and appreciation courses for 110 Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS) Traffic probationers and 60 B.Tech students of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. Faculty development programmes on AI and data science were also organised.

articles.title: Rajiv Gandhi’s security cover was removed deliberately to facilitate his killing: Rahul
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra recalls an incident of slapping a classmate in school after he spoke ill of her uncle Sanjay Gandhi

Former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s security cover was “removed” deliberately to facilitate his assassination, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has claimed in a video conversation with his mother, Sonia Gandhi, and sister, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, while discussing Ms. Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love .

“My position on it is very clear: Papa’s security was removed so that he got killed. Papa’s security removal was not just an accident, it was done on purpose. So that he got killed and the atmosphere was created for him to get killed,” Mr. Gandhi said in the video released on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The V.P. Singh government withdrew Rajiv Gandhi’s Special Protection Group cover in February 1990, after he ceased to be Prime Minister, transferring responsibility for his security outside Delhi to the respective State governments. He was assassinated by a Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam suicide bomber at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, when the State was under President’s Rule.

The assassination continued to have political repercussions, with the Congress withdrawing support from the I.K. Gujral-led United Front government on November 28, 1997, after it rejected the party’s demand to drop DMK Ministers following the Justice M.C. Jain Commission’s interim report on the DMK’s alleged links with the LTTE.

The three Gandhi family members revisited different chapters of their lives in the conversation, including the period following the Emergency and the defeat of Indira Gandhi in the 1977 general election.

The proposal didn't go according to plan and neither did my seventh birthday. The decision in 2004 gave some of us relief but others joy. There was an intention behind withdrawing Papa's security. And even after 500+ pages there are some things Ma has left out of her book. Priyanka and I sat down with our mother to talk through all of it. Going back to those memories brought back the joy, the laughter and even the pain we felt at the time. Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage.
Ms. Vadra recalled slapping a boy at school after he taunted her over the arrest of her uncle, Sanjay Gandhi, following the Emergency.
“After the Emergency, when dadi [Indira Gandhi] lost the election, we moved to a different house. I remember there was a lot of tension,” she said.

Recalling her first day at school after Indira Gandhi lost her election, she said a boy told her, “ Tera chacha jail mein hai, chor hai tera chacha [Your uncle is in jail; your uncle is a thief]. So, I slapped him; then the boy went crying to the teacher and I got a scolding.”

The siblings also recalled how differently they responded to their school environment. While Ms. Vadra described herself as someone who followed rules and was a school prefect, Mr. Gandhi said he was more rebellious and questioned authority.

articles.title: Trump administration set to unveil new tariffs after probe on excess factory capacity: sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Trade Representative’s office is expected to propose ‌new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump’s second term

The Trump administration is poised ​to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected.

The results of the investigation are expected as soon as Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office is expected to propose ‌new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump’s second term.

The duties would partly replace tariffs struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The administration’s tariffs have in part ‌contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November’s midterm elections ‌showed ⁠62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs.

It is unclear what tariff rates ⁠would be proposed. One of the people said that the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies.
USTR has been investigating most of the US’s largest trading partners under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 over what it called ​evidence of excess industrial capacity.

The White House is ‌expected to honor capped tariff rates that were included in finalized US trade deals with partner countries, this person said. These include duty caps of 15% on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19% for Malaysia.

The U.S. also is expected to honor the 20% cap on Trump’s second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a ‌trade truce due to expire on January 10 is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would ​rise to a higher level.
The U.S. Trade Representative’s office and the White House did not respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement.
Ryan Majerus, a former senior Commerce Department trade official, said he ⁠expects a lengthy report that could include differentiated tariff remedies for each of the 16 trading partners.

Majerus, a partner with King & Spalding, said the administration could propose high tariff rates of 15% to 25% on imports from countries deemed to have excess capacity in various sectors. ‌Those levies would stack on top of existing tariffs of 10% or 12.5% imposed under a separate investigation into lax enforcement of anti-forced labor laws.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is in therapy as comeback rally fades
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board

Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.
He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.
But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."
After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."
So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.
Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.
Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.

Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.

He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.

But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."

After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."

So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.

Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.

Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.

articles.title: Cabinet approves ₹11,000-crore scheme to boost CIE manufacturing ecosystem in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian CIE industry is the world’s third-largest, with a market size of ₹97,000 crore in FY 2024-25, yet about 45% of it depends on imports, says Minister
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approved a ₹11,000-crore scheme to boost the country's Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) manufacturing ecosystem.

Addressing the media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister (I&B) Ashwini Vaishnaw said the scheme will run for eight years, starting in FY2026-27, and aims to build indigenous capacity in advanced CIE and position India as a key player in the global market.
The Indian CIE industry is the world's third-largest, with a market size of ₹97,000 crore in FY 2024-25, yet about 45% of it depends on imports, the Minister said.

The scheme includes a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) to set up manufacturing facilities, followed by a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33) and a final year (FY2033-34) to settle incentives for incremental sales made in FY2032-33.

According to an official statement, driven by accelerated growth in infrastructure (roads and ports) and housing, the industry is projected to increase more than double, reaching a market size of around ₹2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30.

The scheme covers seven categories of equipment that are fully or largely imported, including tunnel boring machines, off-highway trucks, excavators, cranes, loaders, piling rigs, and drilling machines. The scheme also provides for establishing a State-of-the-art, dedicated CIE testing facility in the country.
Last month, China announced new export controls on key machinery, including tunnel boring machines, in a move that could adversely impact India's infrastructure development.

According to the statement, the scheme, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), aims to incentivise domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and to establish a dedicated CIE testing facility in the country, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the Global CIE market.

The scheme has two components: a sales-linked incentive and a grant for a CIE testing facility. Under the sales-linked incentive, incentives will be provided on the incremental sales value of eligible CIE equipment and components to approved applicants across two categories — eligible OEMs and Component Manufacturers.

Graded Incentive rates range from 13% to 8% of incremental sales value over five years. Under the grant for a CIE testing facility — a grant of up to ₹375 crore, like Viability Gap Funding — will be given for setting up a dedicated CIE testing facility.

articles.title: YSRCP demands apology over demolition of Anjaneya Swamy temple in Tirupati district for NH expansion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The road alignment could have been changed to save the temple, say YSRCP leaders Velampalli Srinivas and Malladi Vishnu

The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leaders Velampalli Srinivas and Malladi Vishnu have demanded a public apology from the Chandrababu Naidu government and the Endowments Department over the demolition of the centuries-old Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple at Anjaneyapuram, Tirupati district, for National Highway expansion.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday, they alleged that the demolition using bulldozers and earthmovers had hurt Hindu sentiments and amounted to an attack on religious traditions. They questioned why rituals such as Dhyana Adhivasam and Jala Adhivasam, which they said were prescribed under Agama traditions before removing a temple, were not performed.

సనాతన ధర్మం గురించి మాట్లాడే పవన్ కళ్యాణ్‌కు.. దేవాలయాలను కూల్చుతుంటే సనాతన ధర్మం గుర్తురావడం లేదా? పక్క రాష్ట్రంలోని ఆంజనేయస్వామి గుడికి డబ్బులు ఇచ్చానని చెప్పుకునే నువ్వు.. నీ రాష్ట్రంలో ఆంజనేయ స్వామి గుడిని బుల్డోజర్లతో నిర్దాక్షిణ్యంగా కూలుస్తుంటే కనీసం మాట్లాడవా? దేవాలయాలను కూల్చే ప్రభుత్వం కూటమి ప్రభుత్వమని అందరూ తెలుసుకోవాలి. -వెల్లంపల్లి శ్రీనివాస్ గారు, మాజీ మంత్రి #SaveTemplesFromTDP

The leaders argued that the road alignment could have been changed instead of demolishing the historic temple. They pointed out that the government had diverted a road to facilitate a hospital and questioned why a similar option was not considered in this case.

They accused the Endowments Department of failing to protect temples and demanded that the Minister and officials explain their response to the incident. Referring to incidents at temples in Tirupati, Srikalahasti, Srisailam, Simhachalam and Kashibugga, they alleged that the government had failed to ensure the safety of devotees and the protection of temple property and cattle.

Contrasting the present government with the previous YSRCP regime, they said the Srivani Trust had supported the construction of thousands of temples, while the Dhupa Deepa Naivedyam scheme had extended assistance to priests.

రాష్ట్రంలో కూటమి ప్రభుత్వం వచ్చినప్పటి నుండి జేసీబీల ప్రభావం ఎక్కువగా కనిపిస్తోంది. గతంలో టీడీపీ ప్రభుత్వంలో 2014-19లో జేసీబీలు కనిపిస్తే పేద, మధ్య తరగతి వాళ్ళకి ఇబ్బంది ఉండేది. కానీ.. 2024-2026లో జేసీబీలు చూసి దేవాలయాలు కూడా భయపడే దుస్థితి. నిన్న తిరుపతి దగ్గర వందల సంవత్సరాల చరిత్ర ఉన్న అభయాంజనేయ స్వామి గుడిని నిదర్శనంగా కూల్చేయడమే నిదర్శనం. -వెల్లంపల్లి శ్రీనివాస్ గారు, మాజీ మంత్రి #SaveTemplesFromTDP
They also recalled the demolition of temples during the Krishna Pushkarams in Vijayawada under the previous Chandrababu Naidu government, claiming that the YSRCP regime had rebuilt some of them.

Referring to an incident at a Venkateswara Swamy temple in Eluru, they alleged that a trust board member entered the temple wearing footwear and assaulted a priest. They also claimed that pressure was exerted to settle the matter without filing a police complaint.
Questioning the silence of Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan and BJP leaders over the temple demolition, they said coalition partners who spoke about Sanatana Dharma should also take responsibility.

articles.title: AIMIM MLA Akhtarul Iman sparks row with sexist remarks on Muslim women
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita, he said
All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul-Muslimeen (AIMIM) Bihar president and MLA Akhtarul Iman triggered a controversy after a video of him making sexist remarks went viral on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

“Even a tawaif (courtesan) does not sit as decked out and adorned as the bride. Have you no shame, groom? And you, the groom’s father — have you no shame either? Other people are staring at your daughter-in-law; don’t you have any shame? This is the characteristic behaviour of a pig, who invites another male to join him with his female,” said the MLA, who represents the Amour constituency , in the video.

Mr. Iman made the remarks at a religious gathering in Saharsa on Monday (November 23, 2026). He also questioned traditions within the Muslim community, such as muh-dikhai (the ritual of unveiling the bride’s face), the acceptance of gifts during walima (wedding receptions), and excessive spending.

“On one hand, a daughter wears a burqa after marriage, yet on the other, 16-year-old girls walk around with their hair wide open. I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita,” he said.
The AIMIM MLA said while the number of people in society wearing the topi (skullcap) has increased, the dupatta (headscarf) has slipped not only from daughters’ heads but also from their chests.

He added that someone is often tasked with sitting down with pen and paper to record money received from guests, describing this as social posturing and an unnecessary tradition, and urged people to rethink these practices.

The Bihar State Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance of the matter and served him a show-cause notice asking for a reply within a week. Commission member Sajal Jha said he has no right to dictate what women should or should not do, adding that his language is insulting to all women, irrespective of caste or religion.
Bihar BJP media coordinator Danish Iqbal strongly opposed the AIMIM MLA’s statement, saying such remarks cannot be tolerated in India.
“Those who wish to adopt Sharia in place of the Constitution have the option to go to countries like Afghanistan or Pakistan; they are free to leave India and move there,” Mr. Iqbal said.

When The Hindu asked him about his derogatory remarks, Mr. Iman said he had not insulted anyone and had only blamed the groom and the father-in-law, adding that people were making an issue out of nothing.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 25 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita, he said

All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul-Muslimeen (AIMIM) Bihar president and MLA Akhtarul Iman triggered a controversy after a video of him making sexist remarks went viral on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

“Even a tawaif (courtesan) does not sit as decked out and adorned as the bride. Have you no shame, groom? And you, the groom’s father — have you no shame either? Other people are staring at your daughter-in-law; don’t you have any shame? This is the characteristic behaviour of a pig, who invites another male to join him with his female,” said the MLA, who represents the Amour constituency , in the video.

Mr. Iman made the remarks at a religious gathering in Saharsa on Monday (November 23, 2026). He also questioned traditions within the Muslim community, such as muh-dikhai (the ritual of unveiling the bride’s face), the acceptance of gifts during walima (wedding receptions), and excessive spending.

“On one hand, a daughter wears a burqa after marriage, yet on the other, 16-year-old girls walk around with their hair wide open. I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita,” he said.

The AIMIM MLA said while the number of people in society wearing the topi (skullcap) has increased, the dupatta (headscarf) has slipped not only from daughters’ heads but also from their chests.

He added that someone is often tasked with sitting down with pen and paper to record money received from guests, describing this as social posturing and an unnecessary tradition, and urged people to rethink these practices.

The Bihar State Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance of the matter and served him a show-cause notice asking for a reply within a week. Commission member Sajal Jha said he has no right to dictate what women should or should not do, adding that his language is insulting to all women, irrespective of caste or religion.

Bihar BJP media coordinator Danish Iqbal strongly opposed the AIMIM MLA’s statement, saying such remarks cannot be tolerated in India.

“Those who wish to adopt Sharia in place of the Constitution have the option to go to countries like Afghanistan or Pakistan; they are free to leave India and move there,” Mr. Iqbal said.

When The Hindu asked him about his derogatory remarks, Mr. Iman said he had not insulted anyone and had only blamed the groom and the father-in-law, adding that people were making an issue out of nothing.

articles.title: Over 23 lakh vehicles in Keralam have failed to clear Pollution Under Control checks since 2021
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Motor Vehicles department in coordination with State Police has imposed a total penalty of ₹43.2 crore from 2022 to September 30, 2026 for violations related to pollution-control requirements
About 23.9 lakh vehicles in Keralam have failed the mandatory Pollution Under Control (PUC) testing over the past five years.

A total of about 5.74 crore PUC tests were held from the financial year 2021 to September 30, 2026. About 5.5 crore vehicles had passed the test while 23.9 lakh vehicles failed to clear it, according to estimates by the Department of Transport.

About 57.5 lakh tests were conducted from March 2026 to September 30, 2026 and 1.87 lakh vehicles failed the PUC test during this period, said a report furnished by the Transport department before the National Green Tribunal in a case related to a plea for reducing vehicular emissions and promoting environmentally sustainable transport systems in the State.
CAQM report in Supreme Court shows huge gap between policy and groundwork in curbing vehicular emissions

Officials of the Transport department said that vehicles failing the PUC test were required to rectify the defects and undergo retesting before being given permission to resume operations. The pollution monitoring has been strengthened through a network of PUC testing centres that are integrated with the Vahan/Parivahan portal. The department has introduced an Aaadhaar-based mobile OTP system to prevent and reduce fake applications for getting the Pollution Under Control certificate, they said.

The Motor Vehicles department in coordination with the State Police had imposed a total penalty of ₹43.2 crore from the year 2022 to September 30, 2026 for violations related to pollution-control requirements, including vehicles without valid PUC certificates and those with high-emissions. Of the total penalty of ₹43.2 crore slapped, the authorities have collected ₹11.96 crore as on September 2026, according to official estimates.

Health experts have sounded caution against the threats caused by vehicular pollution. “Diesel smoke has been classified as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), which means that exposure at heavy doses over a long period carries a risk of cancer,” pointed out Rajeev Jayadevan, convener of the research cell of the Indian Medical Association, Kerala.
Supreme Court moots allowing only BS-VI-compliant vehicles into Delhi

“Children risk stunting, people with respiratory diseases suffer worsening symptoms, and pregnant women who breathe this air are at higher risk of delivering preterm babies. Air pollution also increases the burden of non-communicable diseases, linked with heart attacks, strokes, high blood pressure, and diabetes,” Dr. Jayadevan said.

articles.title: The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu . The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work.

Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation.

Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

The book is available at The Hindu ’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/ . The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 25 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
